config.mcpEnabled.title: MCP Server: Expose Instances to Agents
config.mcpEnabled.description: Expose the configured Forgejo instances to agent mode as MCP servers: 30 read-only tools by default, plus three write tools that are off by default and each behind its own setting. Turning this off withdraws the server definitions immediately and stops the workspace-repository mapping and the local broker; a client that is already connected keeps the server process it spawned until the window is reloaded.
MCP Write Tools: Create Issue Comment

Let AI agents create issue and pull request comments on your instances through the MCP tool `create_issue_comment`. Off by default. While it is on, an agent can leave public comments under your account: VS Code asks you to confirm each call, but you can turn that confirmation off for the tool, and a client other than VS Code may not implement it at all. Turn this on only when you intend to let the agent write, and read every comment it proposes before approving it.
config.mcpWriteTools.submitPullReview.ti: MCP Write Tools: Submit Pull Review
config.mcpWriteTools.submitPullReview.de: Let AI agents submit pending pull request reviews on your instances through the MCP tool `submit_pull_review`, with the verdict COMMENT, APPROVED or REQUEST_CHANGES. Off by default and separate from the comment switch: approving a pull request can satisfy branch protection, so this is the more consequential of the two. While it is on, an agent can leave public reviews and formal approvals under your account: VS Code asks you to confirm each call, but you can turn that confirmation off for the tool, and a client other than VS Code may not implement it at all. Turn this on only when you intend to let the agent review, and read every verdict it proposes before approving it.
config.mcpWriteTools.cancelActionRun.tit: MCP Write Tools: Cancel Action Run
config.mcpWriteTools.cancelActionRun.des: Let AI agents cancel pending or running Actions workflow runs on your instances through the MCP tool `cancel_action_run`. Off by default and separate from the comment and review switches. This one does not append text — it stops work that is already running, cancelling the run's pending or running jobs; the run has to be triggered again afterwards, which this tool does not do. While it is on, an agent can stop a running deployment, release job or test run under your account: VS Code asks you to confirm each call, but you can turn that confirmation off for the tool, and a client other than VS Code may not implement it at all. Turn this on only when you intend to let the agent stop runs, and check which run it names before approving it.
config.mcpWriteAuditToFile.title: MCP Write Tools: Audit to File
config.mcpWriteAuditToFile.description: Also append the MCP write-tool audit records to `mcp-write-audit.jsonl` in the extension's log folder (VS Code: "Developer: Open Logs Folder"), on top of the Forgejo Toolkit Output Channel. Each record is one JSON line with the caller, instance, repository, target, tool, dry-run flag, body size and digest, result and duration — never the comment text. The file is capped at 1 MB with two rolled files. Off by default: the audit stays in the Output Channel, where it is lost when the window closes.
config.multiWindowLease.title: Notifications: One Polling Window
config.multiWindowLease.description: Poll Forgejo instances and raise notification alerts from only one VS Code window at a time instead of every open window. The mode tries to hand that job to whichever window you are working in; if VS Code's focus state cannot be trusted on your platform, the current holder keeps the lease and the alerts stay with the lease-holding window, and no alert is lost. The other windows stay quiet but still load notifications when you open the view. Turn this off to let every window poll and alert on its own, which uses more requests but is the behaviour before this setting existed.
config.aiPreReview.title: AI Pre-Review
config.aiPreReview.description: Add an "AI Pre-Review Pull Request" action to the pull request diff editor: a chat model reads the pull request and proposes line-level review comments, you pick the ones you agree with one by one, and only those are written as drafts of a pending review. The extension never submits a review — the existing "Submit review" button stays the only way anything becomes public — and an unconfirmed comment writes nothing. Off by default; while it is off the command refuses and no content is sent anywhere. Turning it on sends the pull request's title, its base and head branch names, the changed-file paths with their additions/deletions and status, and the metadata (path, line, author, review state) of existing review comments to the chat model provider you configured in VS Code. What else may be sent — no code at all, the changed lines, the whole diff, or the changed files' own text — is decided by `forgejoToolkit.aiPreReviewPromptScope`, whose default `ask` means: the first pre-review shows one modal naming the provider and what each answer sends, nothing is requested or sent before you answer, and your answer is stored there.
config.aiPreReviewPromptScope.title: AI Pre-Review: Prompt Scope
config.aiPreReviewPromptScope.descriptio: What the prompt may carry during an AI pre-review. This is the only place the egress decision is made and the only place it is recorded: `ask` (the default) means you have not chosen yet, the next pre-review shows one modal naming the provider that would receive the content and what each answer sends, and your answer is written here — so the question is asked once, not once per run. The four stated scopes are `metadata-only` (the model sees no code at all), `changed-lines-only` (the added and removed lines, with the file and hunk headers that keep line numbers unambiguous), `full-diff` (the whole diff, including the unchanged context lines, without the files' own text) and `changed-files` (the whole diff plus the full text of every changed file at the pull request's head version — the most content, and the only scope under which the model can read the code around a change). Every scope is bounded: the changed-file table, the diff and the file texts are cut from the end when they exceed the shared budgets and the file count cap, and every cut is stated in the prompt itself. Only files the pull request changed are ever read or sent — no other file in the repository, no access token, no URL or host name, and never the body of an existing review comment.
config.aiPreReviewPromptScope.enumDescri: Ask before the next pre-review sends anything: one modal names the provider and what each answer would send, nothing is requested, sent or written until you answer, and your answer is stored in this setting.

Send no code at all — only the pull request's title and branch names, the changed-file paths with their line counts, and the metadata (path, line, author, review state) of existing review comments. The model cannot read a single changed line and can only comment on file-level matters.

Send the changed lines of code only — the added and removed lines of each file with its file and hunk headers, and none of the unchanged context lines around them. The cheapest scope under which the model still reads code.
Send the whole diff — every hunk of every changed file, including the unchanged context lines — but not the changed files' own text.

Send the whole diff and the full text of every changed file at the pull request's head version. The most content of any scope, and the only one under which the model reads the code around a change (error handling outside the hunk, callers and conventions elsewhere in the file); the file texts are cut from the end when the shared budget or the file cap is reached.
config.aiPreReviewModel.title: AI Pre-Review: Chat Model
config.aiPreReviewModel.description: Which chat model reviews a pull request, as `vendor/family` or `vendor/id` (an optional `@version` suffix is accepted too) — for example `deepseek/deepseek-flash`, or `copilot/gpt-4o` for the model a provider lists as id `gpt-4o` under vendor `copilot`. Case and surrounding spaces are ignored, and the name is matched against the models VS Code offers, so the first part must be the provider's vendor id and the second its family or model id, as the chat model picker shows them. Leave it empty — the default — and the next pre-review asks which model to use, then writes your answer here; fill it in and every run uses that one model without asking. The extension never picks a model for you and never switches between models: the command "AI Pre-Review: Choose Chat Model" changes this value later. A value that is not one of those forms, or that names a model VS Code does not offer, does not start the run — the message names what you configured and lists the models that are offered, each with its vendor/family and its input token budget — and a model whose input budget cannot hold the feature's instructions is refused too, never silently replaced by another one. The setting matters for privacy, not only for quality: the brief goes to the provider behind the model you name here.
config.prDescription.title: AI: Generate Pull Request Description
config.prDescription.description: Add a "Generate description" control to the create-pull-request form: a chat model drafts a description from the comparison that form is about to submit — the commits between the two branches, with their subjects, bodies, authors and dates, and the path and status of every changed file — and fills it into the description field as an **editable** draft. You still create the pull request yourself; the extension never opens, fills in or submits it for you, and a draft it could not produce leaves the field exactly as you wrote it. Off by default; while it is off the control is hidden and nothing is read or sent. What else may be sent — the changed files' own text at the head branch, or no file content at all — is decided by `forgejoToolkit.prDescriptionPromptScope`, whose default `ask` means: the first draft shows one modal naming the provider and what each answer sends, nothing is requested or sent before you answer, and your answer is stored there. The comparison endpoint reports the changed files and their statuses but no line-level diff, so no hunks are ever sent.
config.prDescriptionPromptScope.title: AI: PR Description Prompt Scope
config.prDescriptionPromptScope.descript: What the prompt may carry when a pull request description is drafted. This is the only place that egress decision is made and the only place it is recorded: `ask` (the default) means you have not chosen yet, the next draft shows one modal naming the provider that would receive the content and what each answer sends, and your answer is written here — so the question is asked once, not once per draft. The two stated scopes are `commits-only` (the branch names, the commits with their subjects, bodies, authors and dates, and the path and status of every changed file — no file content) and `commits-and-files` (the same plus the text of the changed files at the head branch, the most content, and the only scope under which the model can read the code around a change). Both are bounded: the commit list, the changed-file table and the file texts are cut from the end when they exceed the shared budgets and caps, and every cut is stated in the prompt itself. No access token, no URL or host name, and no line-level diff is ever sent.
config.prDescriptionPromptScope.enumDesc: Ask before the next description sends anything: one modal names the provider and what each answer would send, nothing is requested, sent or written until you answer, and your answer is stored in this setting.

Send the branch names, the commits between them (subjects, bodies, authors and dates) and the path and status of every changed file. No file content leaves the machine, so the model can describe what the commits say changed but cannot read the code.

Send the commits and the changed-file list, plus the full text of the changed files at the head branch. The most content, and the only scope under which the model can read the code around a change; the file texts are cut from the end when the shared budget or the file cap is reached.
config.aiProviders.title: AI: Configured Endpoints
config.aiProviders.description: The OpenAI-compatible endpoints this extension may send to, as a list of objects. Each entry needs an `id` (letters, digits, `_`, `-`), a display `name`, and a `baseUrl` used exactly as written apart from a trailing slash — `/v1` is deliberately not appended, because an Azure URL and a gateway's `/openai/v1` would both be made wrong by it. Optional fields: `models` (the models this endpoint has, as `{ id, name }` — a declaration used to fill in the model picker, not a whitelist, so an empty list is allowed), `auth` (`bearer`, `api-key-header` for Azure's `api-key`, or `none` for a local server), `headers` (extra header names, including `api-version`, which is sent as a query parameter), and `localOnly` (this endpoint promises to be on the local machine). Every `baseUrl` must be an absolute `http:` or `https:` URL without credentials in it: a `file:` or `data:` URL and a URL like `https://user:token@host` are refused, and a plain `http://` address is allowed but reported as unencrypted whenever a request goes to it. The API key and every custom header value are deliberately **not** here — they are stored in the editor's secret storage (keys `forgejoToolkit.aiProviderKey.<id>` and `forgejoToolkit.aiProviderHeader.<id>.<headerName>`), and a value written into this setting by hand is ignored rather than sent. Configuring an endpoint here sends nothing by itself: `forgejoToolkit.aiProvidersEnabled` must also be on, and a feature must bind to the endpoint.
config.aiProviders.item.id: A stable id for this endpoint: letters, digits, `_` and `-` only, because the id is part of the key its API key is stored under.
config.aiProviders.item.name: The display name. It is what the consent question, the log and the settings page call this endpoint, so it should identify the machine or service the content goes to.
config.aiProviders.item.baseUrl: The endpoint base URL, used exactly as written apart from a trailing slash. It must be `http:` or `https:` and must not carry credentials; the service's API path (`/v1`, or Azure's own path) has to be part of it, because nothing is appended but `/chat/completions` and `/models`.
config.aiProviders.item.auth: How a request authenticates: `bearer` sends `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, `api-key-header` sends `api-key: <key>` (Azure's spelling), and `none` sends no credential at all (common for a server on this machine). The key itself is stored in the editor's secret storage, never here.
config.aiProviders.item.models: The models this endpoint offers, as `{ id, name }`. This is a declaration rather than a whitelist: it fills in the model chooser and it is what `forgejoToolkit.aiModelBindings` can name, while a model id typed by hand is still accepted. An empty list is not a failure.
config.aiProviders.item.headers: Extra header names this endpoint needs, such as `api-version` (sent as a query parameter rather than as a header). Only the **names** live here; each value is stored in the editor's secret storage under `forgejoToolkit.aiProviderHeader.<id>.<headerName>`. A name that collides with the `auth` style (`Authorization` / `api-key`) is reported and the `auth` style wins.
config.aiProviders.item.localOnly: Whether this endpoint promises to be on the local machine or a private network. A request to a public address is refused while `forgejoToolkit.aiLocalOnly` is on, or while this is on, and nothing is sent.
config.aiProvidersEnabled.title: AI: Allow Requests to Configured Endpoints
config.aiProvidersEnabled.description: The switch that lets any AI feature send content to an endpoint configured in `forgejoToolkit.aiProviders`. Off by default, and independent of everything else: a configured endpoint and a stored API key do **not** enable it, and no AI feature reads a configured endpoint while it is off — so importing a configuration or adding an endpoint can never make content leave the machine on its own. Turning it on is the second of the three separate facts a direct request needs: the endpoint is configured, the key is stored, and you have agreed to send content (which is asked separately, in the feature's own one-time question).
config.aiTransport.title: AI: Model Transport
config.aiTransport.description: Which transport an AI feature asks for a model when the feature has no entry in `forgejoToolkit.aiModelBindings`. `auto` prefers the chat models this editor offers and only considers a configured endpoint when the editor offers none; `vscode-lm` always uses the editor's models; `openai-compatible` always uses a configured endpoint. There is no switching between the two: a transport that fails reports the failure rather than quietly asking the other one, and `auto` never moves content to a configured endpoint that `forgejoToolkit.aiProvidersEnabled` does not allow.
config.aiTransport.enumDescriptions.auto: Prefer the chat models this editor offers; use a configured endpoint only when the editor offers no model, and only when `forgejoToolkit.aiProvidersEnabled` is on and exactly one endpoint can be determined.
config.aiTransport.enumDescriptions.vsco: Always use the chat models this editor offers. With no model available the feature reports that and stops; it never falls back to a configured endpoint.
config.aiTransport.enumDescriptions.open: Always use a configured endpoint. With no usable endpoint, key or binding the feature reports why and stops; it never falls back to this editor's models.
config.aiModelBindings.title: AI: Model Bindings
config.aiModelBindings.description: Which endpoint and model each AI feature uses, as a list of `{ feature, providerId, modelId }`. A binding is the most specific statement there is: it names the destination, so it is used whatever `forgejoToolkit.aiTransport` says (subject to `forgejoToolkit.aiProvidersEnabled`), and a binding that names an endpoint which is not configured, or one that cannot be used, fails and names the entry rather than quietly choosing another endpoint. `providerId` must match an `id` in `forgejoToolkit.aiProviders`, and `modelId` is free text — the endpoint's model name, which does not have to appear in that endpoint's `models` list. An entry naming a feature this build does not know is ignored.
config.aiModelBindings.item.feature: The AI feature this binding is for.
config.aiModelBindings.item.providerId: The `id` of an entry in `forgejoToolkit.aiProviders`. An id that matches nothing fails the run by name instead of resolving to another endpoint.
config.aiModelBindings.item.modelId: The model name to ask for, exactly as the endpoint expects it. It is free text: the endpoint's `models` list is a declaration, not a whitelist.
config.aiLocalOnly.title: AI: Local Endpoints Only
config.aiLocalOnly.description: Refuse any configured endpoint whose host is not this machine or a private network: `localhost`, loopback addresses, the `.local` suffix, and the `10/8`, `172.16/12`, `192.168/16` and `fc00::/7` ranges. The **configured address** is what is checked — no name lookup is made, so a public name that resolves to a private address is not covered (a different threat model), and an address that cannot be read is treated as not local. When it refuses, the feature says which endpoint and which setting stopped it and sends nothing; it never degrades to sending anyway.
config.aiModelRequestTimeoutMs.title: AI: Endpoint Idle Timeout (ms)
config.aiModelRequestTimeoutMs.descripti: How long an endpoint may send **nothing** before a request to it is aborted (default 30000). This is an idle window, not a total limit: a model answer may legitimately take minutes, so a stream that keeps arriving survives however long it takes, and only a silent endpoint is stopped. A second, wider limit applies to the request as a whole — ten times this value — so a stream that dribbles forever cannot hold the window open. Both numbers are written to the debug log, and a value outside 1000–600000 reads as the default.

capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces.descrip: Forgejo Toolkit reads and caches repository state (git worktrees, the extension's cache directory and instance configuration), so it is disabled in Restricted Mode until you trust the workspace.
capabilities.virtualWorkspaces.descripti: Forgejo Toolkit needs real files: it creates git worktrees and maintains a local cache directory for repositories and pull requests.
